title: Bell and Portrait
premise: Wren Thornbury returns to the village of Hollowmere to bury their twin sister Rook, only to find the family house already occupied by aunts and cousins who insist they've lived there for years. Each night at frostfall, a church bell that was melted down in 1911 rings once for every Thornbury still living, and the count keeps rising past anyone Wren can name. The family are echoes, called back by the bell to be counted into the frost, and staying invisible in the village's margins is what has kept Wren uncounted so far. In the end, Wren chooses to be seen—ringing the bell themselves and speaking every forgotten Thornbury name aloud—so the dead are released and the living, found family included, can finally belong without being claimed.
about_author: Vesper Villalobos grew up in a coastal town where three churches shared one silent bell tower, an image that never left them. They write quiet horror about inheritance, small towns, and the people history forgets to count.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Wren arrives in Hollowmere with Rook's ashes and finds the grave already dug—and occupied by a headstone bearing Rook's name, dated eleven years ago. At the wake, aunts and cousins greet them warmly, certain they've always been here. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief curdling into uncanny disorientation as home becomes a place that remembers differently than they do.

chapters.title: One Ring for Every Living Soul
chapters.summary: At frostfall the melted-down church bell rings, and old Aunt Ivy counts aloud, tallying names Wren doesn't know—yet each face matches someone at the table. Wren realizes the 'family' are returned echoes of the dead, summoned by the bell. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror braided with longing, because these impossible relatives offer the belonging Wren never had.

chapters.title: What the Frost Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren researches the 1911 melting and learns the bell tolls to count souls into the frost before winter seals the village; the echoes will fade forever when the count completes. The echoes begin forgetting themselves, and Ivy begs Wren to stay hidden and uncounted. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: rising desperation—saving them means being counted too.

chapters.title: Ring the Bell Yourself
chapters.summary: On the final frost night, Wren climbs the tower, rings the broken bell, and speaks every Thornbury name aloud, claiming the dead instead of hiding from them. The frost releases its count; the echoes depart smiling, remembered at last. Wren stays in Hollowmere with the living neighbors who become true family. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cathartic resolution—belonging chosen over invisibility.
